info.bio: Jane's Addiction, grupo de rock alternativo cuyo origen es Los Ángeles California, fue formado a mediados en los 80 por Perry Farrell, Dave Navarro, Eric Avery y Stephen Perkins. Se les considera uno de los pilares del rock alternativo, y un avance de lo que representarían los años 90 en la música. A pesar de ser un grupo formado en los 80, y que desarrollan la mayor parte de su carrera en esta década, a Jane´s Addiction se los coloca habitualmente en el saco de los grupos de los 90

scenes.name: Funk rock: Chili Peppers, Primus y la Black Rock Coalition
scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
scenes.desc: A los blancos les era mucho más fácil tocar funk y grabar: Jane’s Addiction debutó con un directo, Primus de Les Claypool (devoto de Larry Graham), los Limbomaniacs con Bootsy y Maceo, Praxis. Los Red Hot Chili Peppers de Anthony Kiedis y Flea, con Freaky Styley producido por Clinton (1985), versionaron a Sly, los Meters y Stevie y llevaron a P-Funk al escenario de los Grammy de 1993; pero los creadores del funk rock, como los P-Funk All Stars, no tenían esa libertad. En Nueva York Living Colour de Vernon Reid no conseguía contrato pese a tener a Mick Jagger de fan, y Reid y Greg Tate fundaron en 1985 la Black Rock Coalition: «El rock and roll es música negra y nosotros somos sus herederos», contra el «rock de orientación apartheid». Abrió paso a Steve Coleman, Me’Shell NdegéOcello, James Blood Ulmer o el Kelvynator de Kelvyn Bell.
scenes.family: Funk psicodélico y black rock: Sly, Hendrix

scenes.name: Funk metal, arte y autoparodia
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: A principios de los noventa el metal empieza a perder definición en su periferia: el lite metal se acerca al pop con secciones de cuerda (Damn Yankees), otros grupos meten el funk heredado de las mezclas de punk y funk (Living Colour, Faith No More) cortando el poder del metal con ironía, Jane’s Addiction añade art rock reflexivo y Scatterbrain juega con el género de forma consciente, socavando su autenticidad. Weinstein lo ve como el proceso normal de cambio cultural de un género que conserva su núcleo.
scenes.family: Cruces: rap, funk, industrial, grunge y nu metal

scenes.name: La edad de oro del heavy metal
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El heavy metal renace en los mismos años que la new wave, aprovechando los sellos independientes: Motörhead (puente entre metal, Stooges/MC5 y punk), Judas Priest, Iron Maiden, Diamond Head, Def Leppard y, en EE UU, Van Halen. Entre 1982 y 1985 el subgénero gótico se convierte en «black metal» (Venom, Mercyful Fate, Celtic Frost, Helloween, Bathory). El pop-metal y el shock-rock (Twisted Sister, Mötley Crüe, Joan Jett, Bon Jovi, Savatage); la pompa y el doom (Manowar, Voivod, Saint Vitus, Pentagram); el metal progresivo (Living Colour, Queensrÿche, King's X, Pantera, Joe Satriani) y el «street sound» de Los Ángeles (Guns N' Roses, Jane's Addiction, Faster Pussycat).

podcast.title: Farewell Tour and Lollapalooza (1991)
podcast.body: Jane's Addiction initiated the first Lollapalooza tour, with Perry Farrell using it as a vehicle to commemorate the band's farewell tour. They retired for the first time in August 1991, after the tour's final show in Hawaii. "The fact that Perry needed some kind of hope to commemorate Jane's Addiction's Farewell tour also helped."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First Retirement (August 1991)
podcast.body: Jane's Addiction retired for the first time in August 1991, concluding with the last Lollapalooza tour date on August 28th in Hawaii. "Jane's Addiction, they retired for the first time in August of 1991"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Founding Lollapalooza (1991)
podcast.body: Perry Farrell, the singer for Jane's Addiction, conceived and established Lollapalooza in 1991, an "all-encompassing genre-bending traveling road show" that famously featured a mix of alternative rock and hardcore rap bands. This festival was groundbreaking in bridging racial and social barriers through music. "In 1991, Jane's edition singer Perry Farrell came up with the idea of an all-encompassing genre-bending traveling road show he called Lola Palusa."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Last Ever Tour (1991)
podcast.body: The multi-act bill of the first Lollapalooza in 1991 was put together by singer Perry Farrell specifically to support what was intended to be Jane's Addiction's last ever tour. "the singer for Jane's edition put together a multi-act bill to support what would be the last ever tour for Jane's edition."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lollapalooza (1991) Headliner
podcast.body: Jane's Addiction headlined the very first Lollapalooza show, which began outside Phoenix on July 18, 1991. The festival was originally conceived as their farewell tour. "The lineup featured Jane's addiction, Susie in the bandsheets, living color, nine inch nails, butthole, surfers, raw on-span, iced tea and body count, and fishbone."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lollapalooza 1991 Founding Band
podcast.body: Jane's Addiction was the founding band of the first Lollapalooza tour in the summer of 1991, which featured a diverse lineup of non-mainstream artists and convinced promoters of the commercial viability of such alternative festivals. "Along with founding band Jane's addiction, the line up included Suzy and the band sheets, living color, iced tea and body count, butthole surfers, Rawens band and some weirdo group that was never going to go anywhere called Nine-inch Nails."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Original Lineup's Last Show (1991)
podcast.body: After the 1991 Lollapalooza tour, the band played a couple of contractual shows in Australia and Hawaii, with the very last show of the original lineup taking place on September 26, 1991, at the Aloha Tower in Honolulu. "The date I have for the very last show is September the 26th, 1991 at the Aloha Tower in Honolulu."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Reunions: Some Lasted....and Sadly, Some Didn't ｜ Part 3

podcast.title: Reunion Tour (1997)
podcast.body: Jane's Addiction undertook a reunion tour in 1997, during which Flea from the Red Hot Chili Peppers joined as the bass player. This tour occurred between Dave Navarro's initial tenure and his eventual firing from the Chili Peppers. "There was even a Jane's addiction reunion tour in 1997 that seemed to go all right. I mean, flee even joined up to play bass for the band on that tour."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Perry Farrell Sex Tape Leak (1998) – Multi-Million Dollar Lawsuit
podcast.body: In 1998, a sex tape allegedly featuring Jane's Addiction singer and Lollapalooza founder Perry Farrell was leaked. The tape purportedly showed drug injections, sexual acts, and Satanic references. Farrell responded by filing a multi-million dollar lawsuit. "A sex tape was leaked purportedly showing drug injections, sexual acts, and references to Satan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: 2001 Tour Rider – Audience Laser Pointer Policy
podcast.body: Promoters were required to assure the band that anyone in the audience caught pointing a laser device at the stage would be arrested for assault, reflecting a concern for performer safety and stage integrity. "promoters needed to assure the band that anyone in the audience caught shouting a laser pointing device at the stage would be arrested for assault."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: 2001 Tour Rider – Extensive Medical Services
podcast.body: The rider specified a comprehensive list of medical provisions, including access to a doctor with emergency privileges at the nearest hospital, a throat specialist, a chiropractor, and a masseuse. It also stated that any doctor on call should be given free tickets to the show and explicitly prohibited EMS personnel from being in or near any Jane's Addiction dressing room at any time. "at no time were any EMS people to be in or near any James addiction dressing room."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: 2001 Tour Rider – Luxury Transport
podcast.body: The band's 2001 tour rider insisted on two black stretch limousines with tinted windows, accompanied by a police escort, for their transportation. "A 2001 rider insisted on two black stretch limos with tinted windows and a police escort."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First Public Reunion Gig (2008)
podcast.body: The first proper performance for a paying audience after the original lineup's reunion took place on October 23, 2008, at a bar called Lasita in Los Angeles. "The first proper gig in front of a paying audience was at a bar called Lasita and Los Angeles on October 23rd, 2008."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Reunions: Some Lasted....and Sadly, Some Didn't ｜ Part 3

podcast.title: Original Lineup Reunion (2008)
podcast.body: The four original members of Jane's Addiction did not play together again until April 23, 2008, when they performed a short set following an award ceremony. "Those four guys didn't play together again until April the 23rd of 2008 when they played a short set after an award ceremony."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Reunions: Some Lasted....and Sadly, Some Didn't ｜ Part 3

podcast.title: Alternative Music Evolution Question
podcast.body: Jane's Addiction is used as a reference point to explore the trajectory of music from earlier punk and rock acts, with a specific question about the musical journey "between the jam and Jane's addiction." "What happened between the jam and Jane's addiction?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 1000th Episode of the Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Anchor Rhythm Section
podcast.body: Jane's Addiction, active in the late 1980s and early 1990s, was anchored by the rhythm section of bassist Eric Avery and drummer Stephen Perkins, often cited as one of the best rhythm sections. "James was anchored by bassist Eric Avery and drummer Stephen Perkins."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Band Formation
podcast.body: Eric Avery was the first to join Perry Farrell, with whom he spent time "goofing around." Eric then introduced Perry to his school buddies, guitarist Dave Navarro and drummer Stephen Perkins, both of whom were members of a metal band called Disaster. "Eric was the first guy to join up. He was one of James friends."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Band Naming Origin
podcast.body: The band's name, Jane's Addiction, was derived from "Jane," a friend of Eric Avery described as a "junkie hooker." "Jane being the junkie hooker after which the band was eventually named."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Big Band Drummer Influences
podcast.body: Stephen Perkins' drumming style was heavily influenced by big band drummers such as Buddy Rich and Gene Krupa. This background explains his tendency to play with a "bit of swing," which imparts a looser feel to his overall playing. "His influences were big band drummers like Buddy Rich and Jean Crouppa."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: History of the Modern Drum Kit

podcast.title: Comeback in Alternative Metal
podcast.body: Jane's Addiction was mentioned as an older group that made a comeback in the 2010s, alongside Biohazard and Faith No More, within the Alternative Metal/Alternative Hard Rock scene that was prominent in the 90s. This contributed to the renewed success of heavy bands from the past. "Plus we saw comebacks from older groups like Jane's Addiction, Biohazard and Faith No More to name a few."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 4: The Revivals

podcast.title: Communal Living in East Hollywood
podcast.body: In the 1980s, Jane Bainter, Sergio, Perry Farrell, and approximately half a dozen other individuals shared a Victorian house on Wilton Street in East Hollywood. This communal living situation provided the backdrop for many of the personal experiences reflected in the song "Jane Says." "Jane, Sergio, Perry, and about half a dozen other people shared a Victorian house on Wilton Street in East Hollywood back in the 1980s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Connection to The Jam
podcast.body: The show aimed to explore the connection between The Jam and Jane's Addiction. "What happened between the Jam and Jane's addiction?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Declared Influence
podcast.body: Jane's Addiction is among a partial list of artists and bands who have publicly stated that they have been influenced by Joy Division in some way. "You too, arcade fire, smashing pumpkins, nine inch nails, to pesh mode, sisters of mercy, ministry, chain addiction, the smiths, Bjork, Jesus and Marychain, Moby, primal scream, the Charlotains, Interpol, editors, white lies, Frans Ferdinand. I could go on, but I think you get the point."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's the Big Deal About Joy Division?

podcast.title: Deepening into Alt-Rock
podcast.body: As listeners immersed themselves further into the 1990s alternative music scene, they would often discover bands like Jane's Addiction, signifying an embrace of diverse and influential acts from the era.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What A Drag It Is Getting Old (Musically)

podcast.title: Drug-Oriented Social Circle (Early 1990s)
podcast.body: Dave Gahan was introduced to the social circle that hung around Jane's Addiction by Teresa Conroy, where drugs were consistently available, significantly contributing to his escalating substance abuse. "She introduced him to the people who hung around Jane's Diction, and there were always drugs available with that crowd."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

podcast.title: Early Career Ignored in Los Angeles
podcast.body: In their early days, the band was largely ignored in Los Angeles because their sound did not align with the popular bands of the time, such as Guns N' Roses and Mötley Crüe. "Their sound really didn't fit in with everything else that was happening in Los Angeles. Everyone wanted bands. It sounded like guns and roses and motley crew."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Reunions: Some Lasted....and Sadly, Some Didn't ｜ Part 3

podcast.title: First Drum Set at Bar Mitzvah
podcast.body: Stephen Perkins received his first drum set as a gift for his bar mitzvah. "He got his first set of drums for his bar mitzvah."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: History of the Modern Drum Kit

podcast.title: First Lollapalooza Tour as Farewell
podcast.body: The inaugural Lollapalooza tour in the summer of 1991 was primarily designed as a farewell tour for Jane's Addiction, with the band scheduled to headline and then disband, which largely occurred. "That first Lala Pulusa tour was designed primarily as a farewell tour for Jane's addiction."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Reunions: Some Lasted....and Sadly, Some Didn't ｜ Part 3

podcast.title: Generation X Influence
podcast.body: Jane's Addiction was among the groups that "started to get noticed" at the beginning of the 1990s, helping to coalesce the Alt Rock scene around the tastes of Generation X. "Groups like Jane's addiction and the Pixies are starting to get noticed."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Hollywood Origins and Distinct Sound
podcast.body: Jane's Addiction emerged from the same gritty Hollywood scene as Guns and Roses but developed a distinctly different sound. While they shared a heavy, sometimes Led Zeppelin-esque quality, their overall aesthetics and sensibilities were significantly unique. "Yes, they were heavy and led Zeppelin-esque at times, but there were big differences in both aesthetics and sensibilities."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Impact on Taylor Hawkins
podcast.body: Jane's Addiction profoundly influenced Taylor Hawkins in high school, offering a raw, unpolished alternative to the "blah music" of hair metal. Hawkins viewed them as both "dudes in the poster" and "a mess," "disgusting," "awesome," and "scary," making them his personal equivalent of punk rock. "And then I heard Jane's addiction and it was like, dude, I could play like the dudes in the poster. But they were a mess and they were disgusting and they were awesome and they were scary."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence on Scott Weiland's View of Heroin
podcast.body: In the mid-1980s, Perry Farrell and Jane's Addiction "greatly influenced" Scott Weiland's perception of heroin, contributing to his romanticized view of its connection to rock and roll excess and creativity. "In the mid 80s, I had been greatly influenced by Perry Farrell and Jane's addiction."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influenced by The Stooges
podcast.body: In the 1990s, Jane's Addiction would have inevitably mentioned The Stooges as one of their favorite older bands. "If you were to go back to the 90s and talk to bands like Jane's Addiction or Nirvana in their Prime and ask them about their favorite older bands, one of the names they would inevitably mention would be the stooges."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About The Stooges?

podcast.title: Jane Bainter's Drug Addiction
podcast.body: Jane Bainter, the band's namesake and muse, was a junkie, a fact explicitly referenced in the band's name ("Jane's addiction"). The song "Jane Says" directly details her struggles with drug use. "First, she was a junkie. Farrell and was Jane's addiction."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Jane Bainter's Later Life and Estrangement
podcast.body: By the end of the century, Jane Bainter had achieved sobriety, being clean for eight years, and successfully made her desired move to Spain. However, she eventually fell out with Perry Farrell and the band, resulting in her being snubbed and denied entry to their shows. Furthermore, she has received no financial compensation from anything related to the band or its music. "The good news is that by the end of the century, she had been clean for eight years and did end up going to Spain."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Jane Bainter: Muse and Namesake
podcast.body: Jane Bainter was not only Perry Farrell's ex-housemate and a muse for his lyrics, but she is also the namesake for the band, "Jane's Addiction." She was described as having a posh, aristocratic air and being very intellectual, with her picture featured in the artwork of the band's indie debut album. "Many fans don't know that there really is a Jane who said a bunch of these things. Her name was Jane Bainter."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Jane's Daily Life and Aspirations
podcast.body: Jane Bainter held a day job at an office, but her nights were consumed by shooting up. Despite this, she expressed a strong desire to escape her situation, telling anyone who would listen that she was saving money to run away to Spain, where her divorced mother and new boyfriend had a house in the south of the country. However, her drug addiction made it impossible for her to get herself together enough to make the trip at the time. "She had a day job at an office, but at night she'd come home and shoot up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Jane's Wigs and Personal Integrity
podcast.body: Jane Bainter was known for wearing wigs, a detail included in the lyrics of "Jane Says." Crucially, despite her struggles, the transcript explicitly states that she never resorted to selling her body for sex or drugs, maintaining a level of personal integrity. "Oh, and she wore wigs. However, she never, ever sold her body for sex or drugs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: L.A. Origins and Chart Success
podcast.body: Jane's Addiction, a psychedelic hard rock band from Los Angeles, broke onto the charts in 1990 with two Modern Rock number ones. Their success was a key indicator of the evolving direction of American alternative culture. "A psychedelic hard rock band from Los Angeles called Jane's Addiction."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Live Performance Description
podcast.body: Taylor Hawkins recounted seeing Jane's Addiction perform "seven nights up here in LA" at the John Anson Ford Theater. He was struck by the intensity of their live show, recalling a moment when a "fairy fairy" with green dreadlocks came on stage and immediately confronted a front-row audience member. "I mean, I went to John Hansen for a theater. They did seven nights up here in LA and I was just like, a, a, a fairy fairy came out on stage with green dreadlocks and a woman's hat on and told the first guy in the front row to the second he came out on stage. I was like, these guys are crazy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lollapalooza Conception
podcast.body: Perry Farrell, inspired by the Pixies' performance at Reading on August 26, 1990, conceived Lollapalooza. The festival was initially designed as a farewell tour for Jane's Addiction, masquerading as a broader music festival to get off the ground. "Perry Farrell of Jane's Addiction saw the reaction they got at Reading on August 26th, 1990. He thought to himself, why can't we have this kind of thing in America? And this is when we finally get into how the alt rock nation of the 90s got the North American festival scene kickstarted."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lollapalooza Festival Conception
podcast.body: Singer Perry Farrell conceived the idea for the Lollapalooza Festival in the summer of 1990 after witnessing an enthusiastic crowd at a Pixies set during the 1990 Reading Festival in England, prompting him to want to replicate such an event in the US. "Perry Farrell came up with the concept of the Lala Pulusa Festival in the summer of 1990."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Reunions: Some Lasted....and Sadly, Some Didn't ｜ Part 3

podcast.title: Lollapalooza Founder
podcast.body: As Jane's Addiction prepared for an "indefinite hiatus slash break-up" in 1991, frontman Perry Farrell conceived their final tour as Lollapalooza, an ambitious traveling festival. This festival was designed to bring together diverse acts from "all corners of alternative culture." "frontman Perry Farrell decided their final tour should be an ambitious last hurrah. He launched a novel, traveling festival concert that he called Lala Paloza, smashing together acts from all corners of alternative culture into one eclectic package."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Lollapalooza Founding Band
podcast.body: Jane's Addiction was the founding band of the Lollapalooza festival, which first took place in the summer of 1991.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lollapalooza Inspiration and Headliner Status
podcast.body: Perry Farrell, the band's founder, was profoundly inspired by seeing The Pixies perform at the 1990 Reading Festival, leading him to conceptualize a similar festival for America. Jane's Addiction subsequently headlined the inaugural Lollapalooza tour, which ran from July 18 to August 28, 1991. "The first La La Paloza tour started on July 18, 1991 and ended on August 28. It featured Jane's Addiction as the headliners."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Multiple Reunions without Original Lineup
podcast.body: The band's hiatus was broken several times, specifically in 1997 and from 2001 to 2004, but none of these reformations featured the original classic lineup. "Yes, this hiatus was broken a bunch of times, 1997, 2001 to 2004, but none of these featured the original classic lineup."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Reunions: Some Lasted....and Sadly, Some Didn't ｜ Part 3

podcast.title: Perry Farrell's Stage Presence
podcast.body: Taylor Hawkins recounted witnessing Jane's Addiction's Perry Farrell performing with green dreadlocks and a woman's hat during their "seven nights up here in LA." Farrell's audacious and "crazy" stage persona deeply impressed Hawkins, who considered them "the best at that time." "Perry Farrell came out on stage with green dreadlocks. Woman's hat on and told the first guy in the front row to... The second he came out on stage, and I was like, these guys are crazy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Perry Farrell's Stephen Perkins Myth
podcast.body: Perry Farrell was known for concocting an elaborate myth about Stephen Perkins, claiming the band's first drummer was a Tahitian canary smuggler who died of an overdose, and Stephen was allegedly his twin brother and a former boyfriend of actress Jodie Foster. The narrative explicitly states this myth is not to be believed. "He concocted this myth that the band's first drummer was actually a guy from Tahiti who made a living smuggling canaries."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Production Managed by Kevin Lyman
podcast.body: Before founding the Warped Tour, Kevin Lyman worked as a production manager for Jane's Addiction at Golden Voice and served as a stage manager for their first Lollapalooza road trip in 1991. "There, he got to work as a production manager for groups ranging from Metallica to Jane's addiction."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Profound Influence on Taylor Hawkins
podcast.body: Jane's Addiction significantly impacted Taylor Hawkins in high school, reshaping his musical tastes from older classic rock and new wave to a more alternative sound. He considered them his "punk rock" and became a complete "disciple" of the band, admiring their raw, "disgusting," "awesome," and "scary" aesthetic. "And then I heard Jane's addiction. And then it was like, dude, I could play like dudes in the poster."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Psychic Rhythmic Connection

podcast.title: Reunion Gap - 17 Years, 27 Days
podcast.body: The original lineup's break between their last show in Hawaii and their first proper reunion gig at Lasita spanned exactly 17 years and 27 days. "So how long was that break between Hawaii and the gig at Lasita? Seventeen years and 27 days."

podcast.title: Sampled by Nine Inch Nails
podcast.body: Audio samples from Jane's Addiction were utilized on Nine Inch Nails' debut album, "Pretty Hate Machine." These samples were heavily processed and often made unrecognizable through computer modification by Chris Vrenna. "For example, if you go through that first album, you'll hear samples from Jane's Addiction, Public Enemy, This Mortal Coil, and many others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Deep Dark Secrets of Nine Inch Nails

podcast.title: Sergio: Jane's Abusive Boyfriend/Dealer
podcast.body: The song "Jane Says" mentions an El Salvadorian man named Sergio, who was a real person and Jane Bainter's abusive dealer and boyfriend. He treated her poorly, sold drugs, and sent the money he made back to his family in El Salvador. "The song talks about an El Salvadorian dude named Sergio, another real person. In fact, he was Jane's abusive dealer and boyfriend."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Stephen Perkins as Drumming Influence
podcast.body: Stephen Perkins, the drummer for Jane's Addiction, was acknowledged as a "great drummer" and a significant influence on Taylor Hawkins. Perkins' drumming style was a key component of Jane's Addiction's appeal to Hawkins. "Other influences include Stephen Perkins of Jane's Diction, Great Drummer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Stephen Perkins in Summer Moon
podcast.body: Stephen Perkins, the drummer for Jane's Addiction, also played drums in Summer Moon, a band fronted by Nikolai Fraiture of The Strokes. "Nicolai had a band called Nicolai and another called Summer Moon, which featured Jane's addiction drummer Stephen Perkins."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Following their reunion, Trent Reznor became involved with the band, leading to the recording of some new songs and a subsequent tour in the summer of 2009, known as the "Ninja tour" (NIN and J.A.). "After that Trent Resner got involved, some songs were recorded and everybody went on tour in the summer of 2009."

xref.title: Inspiration for Lollapalooza (1990)
xref.body: While attending the 1990 Reading Festival with his band Jane's Addiction, Perry Farrell was deeply impressed by the atmosphere and had been contemplating a similar annual festival for new bands in North America. The sight of 30,000 Pixies fans singing along to "Debaser" solidified his conviction that his concept for what would become the Lollapalooza Festival would work.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 9

xref.title: Lollapalooza Conception (1990)
xref.body: Perry Farrell, inspired by the crowd's reaction to The Pixies at the Reading Festival in 1990, conceived Lollapalooza. He planned it as a traveling festival, partly to commemorate Jane's Addiction's farewell tour. "Perry Farrell of Jane's Addiction was with some associates at the Reading Festival in the UK, and he was blown away by the crowd singing along to the Pixies as they played their song Debacer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Heroin Addiction Begins (1991)
xref.body: Dave Gahan's heroin addiction began around 1991 after he moved to Los Angeles and became involved with the Jane's Addiction social circle, living a rock and roll lifestyle with his wife, Teresa. A wedding gift they received for their wedding was a lump of black tar heroin. "Heroin was Dave's thing, starting in about 1991."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Lollapalooza 1991 Performer
xref.body: Siouxsie and the Banshees were part of the lineup for the first Lollapalooza tour in the summer of 1991, contributing to the festival's success despite initial ticket struggles, and helping to demonstrate the demand for non-mainstream music. "Along with founding band Jane's addiction, the line up included Suzy and the band sheets, living color, iced tea and body count, butthole surfers, Rawens band and some weirdo group that was never going to go anywhere called Nine-inch Nails."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Lollapalooza 1991 Performer
xref.body: Living Colour performed at the inaugural Lollapalooza tour in the summer of 1991, which proved that a large audience was willing to pay to see a lineup of decidedly non-mainstream bands. "Along with founding band Jane's addiction, the line up included Suzy and the band sheets, living color, iced tea and body count, butthole surfers, Rawens band and some weirdo group that was never going to go anywhere called Nine-inch Nails."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Lollapalooza 1991 Performer
xref.body: Ice-T & Body Count were part of the lineup for the first Lollapalooza tour in the summer of 1991, a tour that, despite initial ticket sales challenges, convinced promoters to continue the festival due to its success in drawing crowds of 20,000 people. "Along with founding band Jane's addiction, the line up included Suzy and the band sheets, living color, iced tea and body count, butthole surfers, Rawens band and some weirdo group that was never going to go anywhere called Nine-inch Nails."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Lollapalooza 1991 Performer
xref.body: The Butthole Surfers performed at the first Lollapalooza tour in the summer of 1991, which, by drawing upwards of 20,000 attendees for a lineup of non-mainstream bands, signaled a shift in music tastes towards alternative acts. "Along with founding band Jane's addiction, the line up included Suzy and the band sheets, living color, iced tea and body count, butthole surfers, Rawens band and some weirdo group that was never going to go anywhere called Nine-inch Nails."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Lollapalooza 1991 Performer
xref.body: Rollins Band was part of the inaugural Lollapalooza tour in the summer of 1991, a successful event that showcased the growing audience for alternative music and prompted promoters to establish it as an annual festival. "Along with founding band Jane's addiction, the line up included Suzy and the band sheets, living color, iced tea and body count, butthole surfers, Rawens band and some weirdo group that was never going to go anywhere called Nine-inch Nails."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Lollapalooza 1991 Performer
xref.body: Nine Inch Nails, described as a "weirdo group that was never going to go anywhere," was part of the lineup for the first Lollapalooza tour in the summer of 1991, which ultimately proved the significant demand for diverse, non-mainstream bands. "Along with founding band Jane's addiction, the line up included Suzy and the band sheets, living color, iced tea and body count, butthole surfers, Rawens band and some weirdo group that was never going to go anywhere called Nine-inch Nails."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Lollapalooza Performance (1991)
xref.body: Nine Inch Nails was an up-and-coming band featured on the bill for the first Lollapalooza tour, which aimed to bring the UK festival experience to America and fill arenas with alternative acts. "It featured Jane's Addiction as the headliners along with up and coming bands like Nine Inch Nails and the Rollins Band along with Ice Tea and Body Counts and the Butthole Surfers and Suzy and the Banshees and more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.body: The Rollins Band was featured on the lineup of the inaugural Lollapalooza tour, which sought to combine various up-and-coming alternative bands to fill larger venues. "It featured Jane's Addiction as the headliners along with up and coming bands like Nine Inch Nails and the Rollins Band along with Ice Tea and Body Counts and the Butthole Surfers and Suzy and the Banshees and more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

"It featured Jane's Addiction as the headliners along with up and coming bands like Nine Inch Nails and the Rollins Band along with Ice Tea and Body Counts and the Butthole Surfers and Suzy and the Banshees and more."

xref.title: Post-Frusciante Guitarists and Internal Struggles (1992-1997)
xref.body: Following John Frusciante's initial departure, the Red Hot Chili Peppers briefly brought in Arik Marshall, who performed with them at Lollapalooza 1992. After Marshall, Jane's Addiction guitarist Dave Navarro was brought in for one album, but his tenure ended unhappily, and he was fired in April 1997. During this period, Anthony Kiedis continued to struggle with sobriety, and Flea was undergoing a messy divorce, adding to the band's stresses. "Dave Navarro was brought in for one album. That's a whole other story that had an unhappy ending."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Red Hot Chili Peppers Guitarist (Post-1992, Fired April 1997)
xref.body: Dave Navarro, guitarist for Jane's Addiction, was brought into the Red Hot Chili Peppers after the 1992 Lollapalooza tour, replacing Arik Marshall. He played on one album with the band, but his tenure was described as "a whole other story that had an unhappy ending." He was ultimately fired in April 1997, paving the way for John Frusciante's return. "James Addiction guitars Dave Navarro was brought in for one album. That's a whole other story that had an unhappy ending."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dave Navarro's Recruitment (September 1993)
xref.body: Dave Navarro joined the Red Hot Chili Peppers in September 1993, replacing Jesse Tobias, who had been with the band for less than a year. Navarro had been courted by several bands after Jane's Addiction disbanded, including an offer from Guns N' Roses to replace Izzy Stradlin, which he declined. Although he initially doubted his suitability for the band's funky style, he was persuaded to join. "Dave joined the Chili Peppers in September 1993 as a replacement for Jesse Tobias, who had been with the band for less than a year."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.body: He was the guitarist for the Red Hot Chili Peppers on their 1995 album, `One Hot Minute`, which was considered inferior to the band's previous work. "Dave Navarro, X of Jane's addiction, of course, was considered to be inferior to what they had accomplished with John Fruciante..."

xref.title: Porn Film Direction and BDSM Product Line (2014)
xref.body: Dave Navarro, known for his work with Jane's Addiction, wrote and directed a porn film titled "Broken" for Evan Seinfeld and Tara Patrick's company, starring Sasha Grey. While he did not perform in any X-rated scenes, he expressed enjoyment for the line of work. In 2014, he collaborated with BDSM company The Stock Room to design a guitar strap that could also function as a multi-purpose BDSM restraint and sex sling. "Dave Navarro, best known for his work with James Diction, wrote and directed a porn film entitled Broken for Evan and Tara's Company."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: NHC (2022) - Most Recent Project
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins' most recent musical project was NHC, where 'H' stood for Hawkins. The 'N' was Dave Navarro and the 'C' was Chris Cheney, both from Jane's Addiction. Taylor described the band's sound as landing "somewhere between Rush and the Faces," and they released the song "Feed the Cruel" in early 2022. "His most recent project was called NHC."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Band Formation and Influence
xref.body: Killing Joke is described as a heavy post-punk group originating from England, which began releasing records in 1980. The band has been a significant influence on a diverse range of artists, including Tool, Nine Inch Nails, Metallica, Nirvana, the Foo Fighters, Jane's Addiction, Marilyn Manson, and Soundgarden. Additionally, Jimmy Page of Led Zeppelin is noted as a massive admirer of their work. "Killing joke has been a big influence on tool, 9-inch nails, Metallica, both Nirvana and the Food Fighters, Jane's Addiction, Marilyn Manson and Soundgarden."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Comeback in Alternative Metal
xref.body: Biohazard was mentioned as an older group that made a comeback in the 2010s, alongside Jane's Addiction and Faith No More, within the Alternative Metal/Alternative Hard Rock scene that was prominent in the 90s. This contributed to the renewed success of heavy bands from the past. "Plus we saw comebacks from older groups like Jane's Addiction, Biohazard and Faith No More to name a few."

xref.body: Dave Navarro, associated with Jane's Addiction, is cited among contemporary musicians who have sold part or all of their back catalog, reflecting a strategy adopted by artists to gain financial freedom.

xref.title: Continued Musical Passion
xref.body: Despite his diverse business and community activities, Bob Ezrin remains a fan of music, demonstrating his ongoing involvement by producing Jane's Addiction's reunion album. "It's busy dude, but he's still a fan of music."

xref.title: Drumming Influences
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins' drumming style was heavily influenced by progressive rock drummers such as Neil Peart of Rush, Stewart Copeland of The Police, and Phil Collins during his time with Genesis. Other influences included Stephen Perkins of Jane's Addiction, Ringo Starr, and his hero, Roger Taylor of Queen. "His heroes were Neil Pirate of Rush, Stuart Copeland of the police, and Phil Collins when he was with Genesis."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Influences & Recognition
xref.body: The Stooges are frequently cited as a major influence by contemporary bands like The White Stripes and The Hives, and by 90s bands such as Jane's Addiction and Nirvana. They also shaped the sound of 80s bands like Sonic Youth and inspired 70s artists like the Sex Pistols, Ramones, and David Bowie to make music. "So the stooges seem to be on everybody's list even though they hardly sold any records in their day and were so messed up that their singer ended up in an asylum."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About The Stooges?

xref.title: Early Punk Era Question
xref.body: The Jam is mentioned in the context of tracing the evolution of music, questioning the connections and influences between different eras and bands, specifically asking "What happened between the jam and Jane's addiction?" "What happened between the jam and Jane's addiction?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Guest Appearances and Collaborations
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins was known for his willingness to assist other bands and artists. He performed on albums by Coheed and Cambria (also touring with them), Eric Avery (Jane's Addiction bassist), Chris Shiflett (Foo Fighter, for Jackson United project), Slash, Ozzy Osborne, and Elton John. "And like his boss and friend, Taylor was always willing to help out other bands."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Heroin Addiction Development
xref.body: Dave Gahan initiated heroin use around 1991, rapidly progressing to a full-blown addiction by 1993. His residence in Los Angeles significantly exacerbated his drug problem, as drugs were easily accessible, especially after his second wife, Teresa, introduced him to the social circle associated with Jane's Addiction. "He had started using heroin in about 1991 and two years later he was a full-blown addict."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Influence of Jane's Addiction
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins cited Jane's Addiction as a major influence that changed his musical direction in high school. Prior to hearing them, he listened to older classic rock and new wave, but Jane's Addiction's raw, "disgusting," and "awesome" style resonated with him, inspiring him to be like them. "And then when I heard Jane's addiction, because I was really... It was all warrant and all that kind of crap, you know."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Influenced by The Stooges
xref.body: In the 1990s, Nirvana would have inevitably mentioned The Stooges as one of their favorite older bands. "If you were to go back to the 90s and talk to bands like Jane's Addiction or Nirvana in their Prime and ask them about their favorite older bands, one of the names they would inevitably mention would be the stooges."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About The Stooges?

xref.title: Inspiration for Lollapalooza
xref.body: Perry Farrell, who attended the 1990 Reading Festival with Jane's Addiction, witnessed The Pixies' performance and the fervent crowd reaction to songs like "Debaser." This scene, with 30,000 fans singing along, was the decisive factor that convinced Farrell his idea for an annual North American festival (Lollapalooza) could succeed.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 9

xref.title: Inspiration for Lollapalooza
xref.body: At the 1990 Reading Festival in England, a set by the Pixies saw a field full of kids "losing their minds," which directly inspired Perry Farrell of Jane's Addiction to create the Lollapalooza Festival in the United States. "What he saw was a field full of kids losing their minds to a pixie set at the 1990 Reading Festival in England."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Reunions: Some Lasted....and Sadly, Some Didn't ｜ Part 3

xref.title: Jane's Addiction as Personal "Punk Rock"
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins was disillusioned with the "blah music" of hair metal (like Warrant) during his high school years. Hearing Jane's Addiction was a transformative experience, as he found them "disgusting," "awesome," and "scary," providing a raw energy that resonated with him much like punk rock did for others. "And then I heard Jane's addiction and it was like, dude, I could play like the dudes in the poster. But they were a mess and they were disgusting and they were awesome and they were scary."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Limited Fanbase, Major Influence
xref.body: Despite not having a large fanbase at the time, The Pixies were highly regarded by influential figures. One such figure was Perry Farrell, founder of Jane's Addiction, who found them amazing and was inspired by their live performance at the Reading Festival. "But there were a few key people who thought they were amazing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Limited Mainstream Breakthrough
xref.body: The Pixies, along with Jane's Addiction, were alternative rock bands that existed before the major punk revival, but despite their influence, they "did okay" without fully breaking through to mainstream attention. "Other bands who would come before, and I'm thinking of the Pixies and Jane's addiction, did okay, but they didn't really break through to the mainstream."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Long COVID Battle and Tour Withdrawal
xref.body: Dave Navarro of Jane's Addiction contracted COVID-19 in late 2021, and although he recovered from the acute phase of the illness, he subsequently became a sufferer of long COVID. His symptoms, including severe fatigue and weakness, persisted for many months, forcing him to withdraw from Jane's Addiction's announced 32-day tour with The Smashing Pumpkins in late 2022. "And although he got through the worst of it, he's become a sufferer of long COVID."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Love Letter in Blood
xref.body: Dave Navarro of Jane's Addiction once wrote a love letter to singer Fiona Apple using his own blood. "Once wrote a love letter to singer Fiona Apple in his own blood."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: 60 Mind Blowing Facts in 60 Minutes: The 5th Edition

xref.title: Move to Los Angeles and Drug Initiation (Early 1990s)
xref.body: After a personal crisis and his first divorce from Joanne Fox, Dave Gahan moved to Los Angeles, where he fully embraced the "Rock God" fantasy. He began using heroin around 1991 and quickly escalated his drug use after meeting Teresa Conroy, who introduced him to the drug-heavy Jane's Addiction crowd. "Right around the time he first started using heroin."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

xref.title: Nikolai Fraiture Solo Projects
xref.body: Nikolai Fraiture has pursued solo musical endeavors, including a band named Nicolai. He also fronted another band called Summer Moon, which featured Stephen Perkins, the drummer from Jane's Addiction. Fraiture also collaborates with his brother on a project that merges music with performance art painting. "Nicolai had a band called Nicolai and another called Summer Moon, which featured Jane's addiction drummer Stephen Perkins."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Ninja Tour Co-Headliner
xref.body: Nine Inch Nails co-headlined the "Ninja tour" with Jane's Addiction, a tour named after the initials NIN and JA. "That was a great name for a tour, NIN, Nine Inch Nails and J.A. Jane's addiction."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Production Managed by Kevin Lyman
xref.body: Before founding the Warped Tour, Kevin Lyman worked as a production manager for various groups, including Metallica, during his time at the LA-based concert promotion company Golden Voice. "There, he got to work as a production manager for groups ranging from Metallica to Jane's addiction."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Recipient of Blood Love Letter
xref.body: Singer Fiona Apple was the recipient of a love letter written in blood by Dave Navarro of Jane's Addiction. "Once wrote a love letter to singer Fiona Apple in his own blood."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: 60 Mind Blowing Facts in 60 Minutes: The 5th Edition

xref.title: Relationship and Marriage to Teresa Conroy (Early 1990s)
xref.body: Dave Gahan became involved with Teresa Conroy, Depeche Mode's former press officer, who introduced him to the Jane's Addiction social circle where drugs were readily available. They were described as "rock and roll soulmates," indulging in the rockstar lifestyle and having a baby daughter together. They married at the Graceland Chapel in Las Vegas by an Elvis impersonator in April 1992. "He also hooked up with Teresa Conroy, the Pesh Mode's former press officer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

xref.title: Returning the Favor to Jane's Addiction
xref.body: Trent Reznor later "returned the favor" to Jane's Addiction by getting involved in their reunion, recording songs with them, and touring together in the summer of 2009. "And it was a good pairing too because that first law of Paloza tour saved Trent Resner from financial ruin in 1991. He was just kind of returning the favor."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Reunions: Some Lasted....and Sadly, Some Didn't ｜ Part 3

xref.title: Rising Prominence in Early 90s
xref.body: The Pixies were identified as one of the groups that "starting to get noticed" at the beginning of the 1990s, playing a role in the coalescence of the Alt Rock scene around the tastes of Generation X. "Groups like Jane's addiction and the Pixies are starting to get noticed."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Sampled by Nine Inch Nails
xref.body: Public Enemy's audio was sampled for Nine Inch Nails' "Pretty Hate Machine." Chris Vrenna manipulated these samples with computers, rendering them largely unidentifiable within the album's tracks. "For example, if you go through that first album, you'll hear samples from Jane's Addiction, Public Enemy, This Mortal Coil, and many others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Sampled by Nine Inch Nails
xref.body: Samples from This Mortal Coil were incorporated into Nine Inch Nails' first album, "Pretty Hate Machine." These were heavily modified and mutilated by computers by Chris Vrenna, making their origins obscure in the final mix. "For example, if you go through that first album, you'll hear samples from Jane's Addiction, Public Enemy, This Mortal Coil, and many others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Deep Dark Secrets of Nine Inch Nails

xref.title: Sampling on Pretty Hate Machine
xref.body: The debut album "Pretty Hate Machine" extensively utilized samples from various artists, including Jane's Addiction, Public Enemy, and This Mortal Coil. These samples were often heavily modified and mutilated by computers, making them largely unrecognizable in the final tracks, a technique Chris Vrenna was particularly skilled at. "For example, if you go through that first album, you'll hear samples from Jane's Addiction, Public Enemy, This Mortal Coil, and many others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Deep Dark Secrets of Nine Inch Nails

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Views on Heroin Culture
xref.body: Weiland openly admitted his love and intrigue for heroin culture, referencing influences from William S. Burroughs, Charlie Parker, the aesthetic of The Rolling Stones, John Lennon's heroin period, and the mid-80s impact of Perry Farrell and Jane's Addiction. He associated heroin with romance, glamour, danger, and rock and roll excess, and was curious about its connection to creativity. "The truth is that I loved heroin culture."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
